title: No deficits in the current generation of players
summary: The current young musicians are socially conscious, communicate well and mature on the road, with none of the old silent groups.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Now, I've heard from you about some of the strengths of having these youngsters.
How about the deficits of having these people like this?
I can't really find any heavy deficits.
And I'll tell you why. For instance, socially and in other ways, this most modern breed are one of the grooviest groups I've ever worked with, as far as just basic people.

Which changes a -- everyone can express themselves quite well. We don't have any more of those groupings where they don't even speak to each other, which used to set music back 20 years at a clip. And they're socially conscious, they're out there, and --
I think it's part of the --
Generation consciousness and humanistic approach and sensitivity to world problems?
Yeah, they seem to be able to handle an audience and anything else.
It's that part of it that gives you great courage. Like, when we go to Europe or anywhere, their approach is so different from what the guys used to do. They
meet people, and even if they don't know the language, they'll learn, spend time with them, much more maturity about them, really.
So I don't find any weaknesses, because I'm not worried on the bandstand, that's for sure. And when I -- I can still be part of these young men, that's definitely good for me. get off, and
